content:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - PagerDuty alert fired: 502 / TLS handshake errors spike for api.redwood.ai (us-west-2)
PagerDuty: Incident PD-7842 triggered (service: api-frontend). Escalation policy: api-prod -> oncall-sre -> eng-runtime.
PagerDuty: auto-assign to oncall-sre.
Incident Bot: Paging @oncall-sre and @DevonP (primary).
Maria Chen: seeing errors in Sentry too. A bunch of 502s and some TLS: handshake_failure logs.
Devon Patel: I’m up, taking it. Any customer reports?
Aisha Gomez: support ticket count spiked ~12 in last 5m, some customers mention TLS errors in browsers.
Samir Rao: LB Target health shows multiple unhealthy targets in tg-api-usw2. Health check path /_health returns 502 on 4 targets.
Devon Patel: ok runbook step 1: confirm LB health + cert status. Samir can you paste ALB/NLB health?
Samir Rao: paste: ```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...tg-api-usw2
{
  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [
    {"Target": {"Id": "i-0a1b2c3d"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Description": "502 from instance"}},
    {"Target": {"Id": "i-0a1b2c3e"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Description": "502 from instance"}},
    {"Target": {"Id": "i-0a1b2c3f"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "healthy"}}
  ]
}
```
Samir Rao: ALB cert status: new cert ARN arn:aws:acm:...:cert/new-cert-2026 attached 2h ago.
Maria Chen: that new cert rollout was part of the morning change for wildcard renewal. Could be related.
Devon Patel: curl from a box in us-west-2 -> ```curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health``` returns TLS handshake error: "SSL: certificate subject name does not match target host name" and then 502s from LB when it negotiates.
Incident Bot: Relevant runbook: "LB failures / TLS surprises" -> https://runbooks.redwood/infra/lb-tls-failures
Devon Patel: quick mitigation options: 1) roll ALB back to previous cert, 2) deregister unhealthy targets and drain then re-register, 3) shift traffic to fallback region (us-east-1) if DNS weighted failover is configured. Which is fastest?
Samir Rao: rolling cert back is quickest if cert is the cause. We have previous cert ARN arn:aws:acm:...:cert/prev-2024 available.
Aisha Gomez: note — some corporate customers hitting our API via older TLS stacks reported failures; might be cert chain ordering issue.
Maria Chen: I'm seeing a spike in 502s specifically on POST /v1/generate and some TLS alerts for SNI mismatch.
Devon Patel: I'm going to test reattaching the previous cert to the ALB listener in a minute. Samir, stand by to watch target health.
Samir Rao: watching. Also checking target logs. Instances show nginx returning 502 because backend returns empty response (kv cache issues maybe).
Devon Patel: stopping the cert switch if any negative. I'll do it during a small maintenance window: switching listener cert to previous ARN now.
Incident Bot: Deploy bot notice: config change requested by Devon Patel on ALB listener (not automated)
Devon Patel: ```aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:aws:...listener --certificates CertificateArn=arn:aws:acm:...:cert/prev-2024```
Samir Rao: I see handshake errors drop off immediately in metrics. TLS handshake failure rate down 80% within 30s.
Maria Chen: Sentry errors for TLS decreasing. Support volume stabilizing. :white_check_mark:
Aisha Gomez: sending a short note to affected customers that we mitigated root cause and we're investigating follow-up steps.
Devon Patel: next steps: 1) keep previous cert attached for now, 2) run health checks on targets and restart services on instances with persistent 502, 3) investigate the cert chain and CSR used for new cert. Samir, can you re-register or restart services on the 2 unhealthy instances?
Samir Rao: re-registering targets and restarting app on i-0a1b2c3d, i-0a1b2c3e. ```sudo systemctl restart redwood-api && tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/api.log``` Results: app came up, health endpoint returning 200. Target group now 6/6 healthy.
Devon Patel: great. Maria can you draft incident summary + customer impact and flag whether any SLA targets were missed?
Maria Chen: putting initial impact: ~5% of requests in us-west-2 got 502/TLS errors between 14:02-14:07 UTC, approx 12 customer tickets, no data exfiltration. I'll add numbers from metrics soon.
Incident Bot: PagerDuty: PD-7842 acknowledged by oncall-sre (Devon Patel).
PagerDuty: Escalation cancelled after ack.
Devon Patel: I'm going to hand off monitoring to oncall-sre for the next hour; leaving a follow-up action item to rotate cert issuance pipeline and add a canary before auto-attaching new certs.
oncall-sre: acknowledged, monitoring dashboards up. If anything flares I'll page again.
Aisha Gomez: I'll update customers who've opened tickets with an ETA for a postmortem.
Samir Rao: I'll open a task to validate ACM cert chain ordering and test it in staging with older TLS clients.
Maria Chen: writing incident timeline now. Will include: cause suspected (bad cert packaging), mitigation (rolled back to previous cert + restarted app on unhealthy targets), customer impact, follow-ups.
Devon Patel: thanks all. Closing this PD incident now but keeping thread open for postmortem notes.
PagerDuty: PD-7842 resolved by Devon Patel.
Incident Bot: Incident closed in PagerDuty. :white_check_mark:
Maria Chen: linking draft postmortem here in ~30m.
Devon Patel: handing off full writeup to Maria. I'm available for follow-ups.
oncall-sre: final check 14:25 UTC — metrics stable, no TLS alerts, LB targets all healthy.
Maria Chen: last note — reduce ACM auto-attach privileges until we have a canary verification step.
Devon Patel: agreed. I'll add to infra backlog.
Aisha Gomez: closing support loop, notifying affected customers that issue is resolved. :lock_with_ink_pen:
Maria Chen: thread summary done, will file postmortem and link to this thread.
